EST.1.1-2.text: Xerxes rules 127 provinces from his throne in Susa

EST.1.3-4.text: Xerxes shows his riches to his officials for 180 days

EST.1.5-6.text: Xerxes gives a seven-day feast for all people in Susa

EST.1.7-8.text: At the feast, the king lets every man drink freely

EST.1.9-11.text: Xerxes orders eunuchs to bring Queen Vashti to him

EST.1.12-12.text: Queen Vashti refuses to come, and the king is furious

EST.1.13-15.text: Xerxes asks his advisors what to do about Vashti

EST.1.16-18.text: Memucan warns that wives will despise husbands

EST.1.19-20.text: Memucan advises a decree to remove Vashti as queen

EST.1.21-22.text: Xerxes sends letters that every man must rule his home

EST.2.1-2.text: Xerxes’ attendants suggest a search for young women

EST.2.3-4.text: Xerxes plans to choose a new queen from young women

EST.2.5-6.text: Mordecai is a Jewish man living in Susa

EST.2.7-7.text: Mordecai raises his cousin Esther as his own daughter

EST.2.8-9.text: Esther is taken to the palace and Hegai favors her

EST.2.10-11.text: Esther does not reveal her people, as Mordecai said

EST.2.12-13.text: Each young woman receives a year of beauty treatments

EST.2.14-14.text: A young woman goes to the king and then to a second harem

EST.2.15-16.text: Esther gains favor and goes to King Xerxes

EST.2.17-18.text: Xerxes makes Esther queen and holds a great banquet

EST.2.19-20.text: Esther still keeps her people secret, as Mordecai said

EST.2.21-21.text: Two guards plan to kill King Xerxes

EST.2.22-23.text: Mordecai reports the plot and the two guards are hanged

EST.3.1-2.text: The king honors Haman, but Mordecai will not bow

EST.3.3-4.text: The king’s servants tell Haman that Mordecai disobeys

EST.3.5-6.text: Haman is angry and plans to destroy all the Jews

EST.3.7-7.text: Haman casts lots to choose a day and month

EST.3.8-9.text: Haman asks King Xerxes to destroy the Jews

EST.3.10-11.text: The king gives Haman his ring and power over the Jews

EST.3.12-13.text: Haman’s order to kill all the Jews is written and sent

EST.3.14-15.text: The edict is sent out and Susa is in confusion

EST.4.1-3.text: Mordecai and the Jews mourn because of the edict

EST.4.4-5.text: Esther sends Hathach to ask Mordecai what is wrong

EST.4.6-8.text: Mordecai asks Esther to plead with the king for the Jews

EST.4.9-12.text: Esther tells Mordecai she may not go to the king

EST.4.13-14.text: Mordecai tells Esther she must not stay silent

EST.4.15-17.text: Esther asks the Jews to fast and agrees to go

EST.5.1-2.text: The king welcomes Esther with his gold scepter

EST.5.3-4.text: Esther invites the king and Haman to a banquet

EST.5.5-6.text: At the banquet the king asks Esther what she wants

EST.5.7-8.text: Esther invites the king and Haman to a second banquet

EST.5.9-11.text: Haman is angry at Mordecai and boasts to his friends

EST.5.12-13.text: Haman says Mordecai’s presence spoils all his joy

EST.5.14-14.text: Haman’s wife and friends tell him to build a gallows

EST.6.1-3.text: The king learns that Mordecai was never rewarded

EST.6.4-6.text: The king asks Haman how to honor a man

EST.6.7-9.text: Haman describes how the king should honor a man

EST.6.10-11.text: The king orders Haman to honor Mordecai

EST.6.12-14.text: Haman goes home in grief and is taken to the banquet

EST.7.1-2.text: The king asks Esther again what she wants

EST.7.3-5.text: Esther asks the king to save her and her people

EST.7.6-6.text: Esther names Haman as the enemy

EST.7.7-7.text: The angry king leaves, and Haman begs Esther for his life

EST.7.8-8.text: The king sees Haman fall on Esther’s couch

EST.7.9-10.text: Haman is hanged on the gallows he made for Mordecai

EST.8.1-2.text: The king honors Esther and Mordecai

EST.8.3-4.text: Esther weeps and begs the king to stop Haman’s plan

EST.8.5-6.text: Esther asks the king to cancel Haman’s letters

EST.8.7-8.text: The king lets Mordecai write a new decree for the Jews

EST.8.9-9.text: Mordecai’s orders are written to all 127 provinces

EST.8.10-12.text: The decree lets the Jews defend themselves on one day

EST.8.13-14.text: Couriers carry the decree to every province quickly

EST.8.15-17.text: Mordecai leaves the king, and the Jews rejoice

EST.9.1-2.text: On the thirteenth day, the Jews overpower enemies

EST.9.3-5.text: Officials help the Jews, who defeat all enemies

EST.9.6-10.text: The Jews kill 500 men and Haman’s ten sons in Susa

EST.9.11-12.text: The king asks Esther what more she wants

EST.9.13-14.text: Esther asks for one more day, and Haman’s sons are hanged

EST.9.15-16.text: The Jews kill more enemies in Susa and the provinces

EST.9.17-17.text: The Jews rest on the fourteenth day with feasting

EST.9.18-19.text: Jews in Susa and in villages rest on different days

EST.9.20-22.text: Mordecai tells the Jews to celebrate two days each year

EST.9.23-25.text: The Jews continue the custom because Haman’s plot failed

EST.9.26-28.text: The days are called Purim and are to be kept every year

EST.9.29-29.text: Esther and Mordecai write a second letter about Purim

EST.9.30-32.text: Mordecai sends letters to confirm the days of Purim

EST.10.1-2.text: King Xerxes taxes the land; Mordecai’s deeds are recorded

EST.10.3-3.text: Mordecai is second only to King Xerxes and helps the Jews
